title: An autonomously reproducing cell built from defined components

concept.text: The proposed innovation is a cell assembled from individually specified components that can maintain itself, reproduce and pass its reproductive capacity to its descendants. Its genome would coordinate gene expression, energy metabolism, membrane growth and division, while each generation would regenerate the machinery needed for subsequent generations. Continued reproduction would depend on specified environmental inputs, with the cell itself producing and assembling its essential cellular machinery.

Defined components can include individually purified natural proteins, ribosomes, nucleic acids and lipids whose identities and concentrations are known. This construction approach allows researchers to control the starting composition without requiring every initial ingredient to be synthesized from simple chemicals. The central capability is achieving a self-maintaining reproductive cycle from that defined starting system.

significance.text: Achieving this capability would provide an experimentally manipulable, sufficient chemical implementation of cellular life. Researchers could vary known ingredients and genetic instructions to investigate how replication, metabolism, compartment growth and inheritance become mutually sustaining. Control over the identity and concentration of starting components would make the requirements for cellular organization directly testable.

Synthesis of the proposed impact suggests that such cells could become platforms for studying minimal biological requirements and designing specialized organisms for medicine or manufacturing. Those applications would require additional advances in functional design, containment, reliability and scale. Reproductive autonomy alone would leave substantial application-specific engineering work.

Interpretive synthesis places an important boundary on the origins-of-life implications. A successful construction would establish that its particular ingredients and conditions suffice for cellular reproduction. Establishing how life actually originated on Earth would require separate historical and geochemical evidence. The supplied material also provides no historical comparison set from which to calibrate the magnitude of the innovation against earlier scientific revolutions.

missing_breakthrough.text: The unresolved capability is sustained regeneration of the complete reproductive system. Genome copying, gene expression, energy supply, membrane growth and division must remain coupled as cellular contents are consumed, damaged and partitioned into descendants. Beginning with purified functioning machinery bypasses much of its biosynthesis and assembly. Reproducing that machinery within the system adds a further engineering burden, illustrated by the reported dependence on supplied enzymes, ribosomes and lipids.

The July 2026 system identifies concrete metabolic and biosynthetic gaps. Its authors report very limited metabolism and an inability to make ribosomes, and they associate greater metabolic independence with a larger genome. Overcoming these dependencies would require the genetic instructions, substrates, energy provision and assembly processes needed to replace essential machinery over successive generations. Ribosome production is especially consequential because protein synthesis depends on the very machinery that descendants must replenish.

Reproductive integration also remains incomplete in the reported experiments. The multigeneration protocol uses mechanical extrusion for division and fresh feeder liposomes for replenishment. A separate genetically encoded division experiment still requires externally supplied streptavidin and a linker. Sustained adaptive evolution introduces another requirement. The authors identify spontaneous generation of mutations as a further step beyond their selection experiment using an introduced beneficial promoter variant.

current_state.text: A bioRxiv preprint by Nathaniel J. Gaut and colleagues, posted on 2 July 2026, reports a chemically defined synthetic-cell system integrating genome replication, gene expression, feeding, membrane growth and division. The validated review assessed supplied manuscript passages describing these experiments. The reported integration represents progress toward the proposed innovation, while continued dependence on external machinery and interventions leaves autonomous propagation unestablished by this evidence.

The manuscript reports five generations of synthetic-cell cycling. In the described protocol, cells are mechanically divided by extrusion after 12 hours and mixed with a fresh population of feeder liposomes to begin another generation. The feeders supply complex machinery, including RNA polymerase, Phi29 polymerase and the PURE translation system. These experiments therefore report multigeneration replication and gene expression with recurring external replenishment and mechanically assisted division.

A separate experiment combines replication, feeding and genetically encoded division, with DNA assays on daughter fractions. Division is induced after feeding through the addition of externally supplied streptavidin and a biotin-FLAG antibody linker. This experiment supports reported integration of growth and division under those conditions. Serial propagation using that division mechanism without the stated external assistance remains to be demonstrated.

The authors explicitly report that their synthetic cells have very limited metabolism and cannot make ribosomes. They also report selection of an introduced beneficial promoter variant. Their discussion identifies spontaneous emergence of mutations as a subsequent step toward sustained Darwinian evolution. The selection result establishes a narrower evolutionary capability than the sustained mutation-and-selection process envisioned for the completed innovation.

The available assessment is limited to the preprint's reported results, methods and explicit dependencies. All three supplied text extractions are truncated, with the reviewed PDF extraction ending during page 41. Figure images and underlying data were unavailable for inspection, leaving figure-level validity and independent reproducibility unassessed. Earlier research described an access failure, but the later review had inspectable manuscript passages supporting the limitations summarized here. The supplied record contains no bounded freshness-search results establishing the field's state through 1 November 2026, so these findings remain a dated account of the July report.

completion_criteria.text: A proposed convincing demonstration would begin with a fully specified starting composition and reproduce the system in independent laboratories. Researchers would propagate descendants through many serial transfers using an explicitly defined nutrient supply, without periodically replenishing complex cellular machinery. Before testing, the protocol would specify the number of generations, transfer dilutions, nutrient composition, permitted environmental interventions and criteria for continued propagation. These are proposed operational criteria whose thresholds would need justification.
completion_criteria.label: Independent laboratories reproduce serial propagation from fully specified starting compositions

completion_criteria.text: A proposed autonomy test would track whether descendants synthesize and assemble the machinery needed for further reproduction, including essential enzymes and ribosomes, while replacing membrane material and maintaining energy supply. Material and energy accounting, together with measurements across transfers, would establish whether sustained performance can be attributed to regenerated cellular components. The experiment should explicitly account for the carryover of starting machinery and any externally supplied cellular components.
completion_criteria.label: Descendants regenerate reproductive machinery with material and energy accounting

completion_criteria.text: A proposed inheritance-and-evolution demonstration would show faithful transmission of genetic information alongside the spontaneous appearance and inheritance of variants that undergo sustained adaptive selection. This requirement extends the preprint's reported selection of an introduced beneficial promoter variant and addresses the authors' stated next step of enabling spontaneous mutations. The duration and breadth needed to make that demonstration convincing remain to be specified.
completion_criteria.label: Spontaneous heritable genetic variants undergo sustained adaptive selection

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reporting boundaries would include the range of nutrient conditions, environmental settings, transfer procedures and generation counts under which reproduction succeeds, together with observed failure modes. Finite experiments would establish sustained reproduction and evolution across the demonstrated conditions. Indefinite persistence and universality would remain beyond what those tests could establish.
completion_criteria.label: Report demonstrated reproduction conditions, experimental limits and failure modes

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis identifies MIC-06, A predictive whole-cell model for microbial design, as the closest methodological complement. Such a model could help explain or design the coupling of metabolism, gene expression and reproduction in a defined cell. MIC-01 centers on experimentally constructing a self-regenerating reproductive system, while MIC-06 centers on predictive modeling capability.

Roster-based synthesis links MIC-02, A predictive theory of microbial communities, and MIC-10, Programmable microbial consortia for durable ecosystem functions, through the possibility of using defined cells as controllable community members. MIC-02 concerns prediction across interacting populations, and MIC-10 concerns engineering durable collective functions. Both retain questions about ecological interactions and stability beyond constructing an individual reproducing cell.

Roster-based synthesis connects MIC-04, Reliable nitrogen-fixing microbial partnerships for major cereal crops, and MIC-07, Programmable, reversible living therapies in the human microbiome, to possible future uses of designed cells. Their completion would additionally require reliable host interactions and application-specific performance. MIC-12, A causal map from microbial metabolites to host phenotypes, could help identify and evaluate functions relevant to such uses, while retaining its focus on causal metabolite–host relationships.

Roster-based synthesis links MIC-03, Routine experimental access to microbial dark matter, through shared interests in cellular requirements and experimentally tractable systems. MIC-03 concerns access to existing microbial diversity whose cultivation or study remains difficult. MIC-01 concerns constructing a reproductive system from a defined set of starting components.

Roster-based synthesis associates MIC-05, A general platform for targeted, adaptable phage treatment, MIC-08, Broadly effective control of bacterial antibiotic persistence, and MIC-09, Forecasting horizontal gene transfer and resistance spread in microbial communities, with potential experimental uses of controlled cellular systems. Their central challenges concern phage treatment, persistence physiology and community-level genetic exchange, respectively. Achieving cellular reproduction from defined components would leave those capabilities to be established separately.

Roster-based synthesis gives MIC-11, Quantifying how environmental viruses control biogeochemical fluxes, a more indirect connection. Defined cellular systems might support controlled studies of selected virus–cell interactions, while MIC-11 requires quantitative understanding that connects viral activity to environmental processes and ecosystem-scale fluxes.

unresolved_issues: The supplied record does not establish whether later work changed the field's state through 1 November 2026.
The preprint's figure-level results, underlying data and independent reproducibility remain unassessed in the supplied review. Truncated extractions also limit completeness.
The proposed completion criteria still require justified definitions of generation count, transfer dilution, permitted nutrient complexity and environmental intervention.
The evidence does not establish sustained propagation with regeneration of essential machinery and without recurring complex-machinery replenishment.
Serial reproduction using the genetically encoded division mechanism without its reported external assistance remains to be demonstrated.
Sustained adaptive evolution involving spontaneously arising heritable variants remains beyond the reported introduced-variant selection result.

brief.title: A cell built from known parts that keeps reproducing
possible: Scientists could assemble a cell from known ingredients that keeps itself running and produces descendants able to do the same. Its DNA, the molecule carrying genetic instructions, would coordinate growth and reproduction. With a defined food supply, each generation would rebuild the machinery the next needs.
why: Researchers could change individual ingredients and genetic instructions to test what makes cellular life sustain itself. This would make the minimum requirements for life directly testable and provide a starting point for designing specialized cells for medicine or manufacturing.

sources.who: Nathaniel J. Gaut and colleagues, University of Minnesota
sources.showed: They reported five generations of DNA copying and growth, using mechanical division and fresh supplies of cellular machinery. A separate experiment linked growth to division controlled by genes, with outside assistance.
sources.quote:
Finally, coupling genetically encoded growth and division 
resulted in synthetic cells that can feed, grow, and divide.
sources.cited_for: This work brings several processes needed for reproduction together in a system assembled from known ingredients.
sources.not_established: The preprint does not demonstrate descendants continually replacing their essential machinery and reproducing without repeated outside assistance.

sources.who: Ana María Restrepo Sierra and colleagues
sources.showed: They built membrane compartments in which genetic instructions supported protein production, DNA copying and production of fats used in cell membranes.
sources.quote:
Here, we engineer phospholipid vesicles that can operate three essential 
functions, namely transcription-translation of a partial genome, self-replication of this DNA program, and 
membrane synthesis.
sources.cited_for: This work connects copying genetic instructions with making material for a cell's outer covering.
sources.not_established: Combining these functions does not establish repeated cell division or replacement of the complete reproductive machinery.

sources.showed: They made and assembled functional ribosomes, the machinery that builds proteins, outside living cells. Their reaction used material extracted from bacteria.
sources.quote: In this study, we report the successful realization of ribosome biogenesis in vitro.
sources.cited_for: This work addresses the need for descendants to make their own protein-building machinery.
sources.not_established: Ribosome production in a bacterial extract does not establish a reproducing cell assembled entirely from individually specified ingredients.

sources.showed: They regenerated all thirty supporting proteins needed by a bacterial protein-making system. Simultaneous regeneration required genes concentrated on a surface.
sources.quote:
Here, we demonstrate the autonomous and simultaneous 
biogenesis of all thirty proteins of the translation machinery of E. coli  in a reconstituted 
transcription-translation system.
sources.cited_for: This work shows that newly made supporting proteins can feed back into the machinery that produces them.
sources.not_established: Regenerating these proteins does not establish replacement of ribosomes or sustained reproduction of a complete cell.

sources.who: Zhanar Abil, Ana María Restrepo Sierra and colleagues
sources.showed: They sustained DNA copying inside membrane compartments over repeated rounds. Genetic changes accumulated that gave the copying system a selective advantage.
sources.quote: The self-replicator can survive across multiple rounds of replication-coupled transcription-translation reactions in liposomes and, within only ten evolution rounds, accumulates mutations conferring a selection advantage.
sources.cited_for: This work demonstrates adaptive evolution of a DNA-copying system inside membrane compartments.
sources.not_established: Evolution of the DNA-copying system does not establish evolution of a whole cell that rebuilds its machinery and reproduces.

shown: Gaut and colleagues report the broadest integration described here: cells assembled from known ingredients that copy DNA, make proteins, feed, grow and divide. Their result is a preprint, and independent reproduction remains to be demonstrated.
missing: Descendants have yet to rebuild the complete reproductive system, including ribosomes, while maintaining their energy supply.
Repeated reproduction has yet to continue without mechanical division or externally supplied division aids and replacement machinery.
Spontaneous inherited changes have yet to drive sustained adaptation in a complete cell that maintains its own reproduction.

milestones.label: Independent laboratories reproduce continued cell reproduction from known ingredients
milestones.explanation: Independent laboratories would have to sustain descendants through repeated transfers from fully specified ingredients, without replacing complex machinery. This would establish that continued reproduction is reproducible.

milestones.label: Descendants rebuild reproductive machinery with accounted materials and energy
milestones.explanation: Measurements would have to track materials and energy as descendants rebuild essential machinery, membranes and energy supply. This would distinguish self-renewal from survival on starting components.

milestones.label: Spontaneous inherited changes support sustained adaptation
milestones.explanation: Descendants would have to inherit genetic instructions faithfully while new, spontaneous variants undergo sustained selection. This would extend adaptation beyond a beneficial change introduced by researchers.

milestones.label: Successful reproduction conditions and failure modes are reported
milestones.explanation: Experiments would have to establish which food supplies, environments and transfer procedures sustain reproduction, and where it fails. This would define the demonstrated capability without claiming indefinite survival.

uncertain: How many generations and how much dilution would convincingly rule out dependence on the starting machinery?
What nutrient complexity and environmental assistance should count as compatible with reproductive autonomy?
How long and across what range of conditions must inherited adaptation persist to demonstrate sustained evolution?

page.title: Autonomous reproduction of chemically defined synthetic cells
page.definition: A cell assembled from molecules of known identity and concentration grows, copies its genome and divides, with descendants rebuilding the machinery needed to repeat the cycle. Its genome carries genetic instructions, and its environment supplies specified nutrients and energy.

goal.need: JCVI-syn3.0, reported on 25 March 2016, contained 473 genes, including 149 with unknown biological functions. Constructing a reproducing cell from specified molecules would provide an experimental test of which components and interactions suffice for cellular reproduction, supporting Build-a-Cell’s goal of understanding the functions of every constituent.

figures.caption: Genes in JCVI-syn3.0 as reported on 25 March 2016
figures.note: The functional assignments describe the 2016 publication.

statements.quote: We wish to create an organism for which all molecules are understood from a first order functional perspective
the SynCell Asia Initiative outlines a strategy for developing core functional modules followed by their systems-level integration
statements.context: The stated objective is building a living cell from scratch.

completion.title: A defined synthetic cell completes ≥10 growth–division cycles with endogenous ribosome regeneration.
completion.criterion: A bottom-up synthetic cell completes ≥10 continuous, coordinated growth–division cycles, with endogenous, genome-encoded ribosome regeneration replacing the external cell-free expression system. The starting cell has a specified molecular composition, and descendants retain the capacity to repeat the reproductive cycle.
completion.set_by: SynCell Asia Initiative, AutoCell stage of its CAS/NSFC-supported roadmap, stated in the coordinating Chinese Academy of Sciences announcement of 28 May 2026.
completion.threshold_quote: Specifically, the aim is for AutoCell to complete ≥10 continuous, coordinated growth-division cycles
completion.basis: This is the reproduction target within SynCell Asia’s AutoCell stage. Endogenous ribosome regeneration addresses dependence on externally supplied protein-synthesis machinery. The roadmap also sets objectives for evolution under environmental selection and the formation of synthetic cell communities.

milestones.title: An encapsulated cell-free system replicates DNA.
milestones.criterion: DNA is copied inside an encapsulated cell-free system. Abil et al., published on 22 October 2024, sustained DNA replicators for at least five cycles using supplied PURE protein-synthesis machinery and freeze–thaw mixing. Restrepo Sierra et al., published on 13 February 2026, combined DNA copying and membrane-lipid synthesis in 2.9 ± 1.3% of liposomes at 34 °C across eight biological replicates (mean ± s.e.m.).
milestones.set_by: Rothschild et al.’s 2024 roadmap, Box 2, stage 1, endorsed by Build-a-Cell on its introductory reading page.
milestones.threshold_quote: Accomplish DNA replication in an encapsulated cell-free system

milestones.title: A cell-free system synthesizes functional ribosomes and its remaining translation apparatus.
milestones.criterion: A cell-free system synthesizes functional ribosomes and the remaining machinery for translating genetic instructions into proteins. Kosaka et al., published on 8 January 2025, detected translation by mixed, purified nascent ribosomal subunits in three independent experiments using bacterial extract. Schwarz-Schilling et al., published on 30 December 2025, simultaneously regenerated 30 translation proteins on surface-bound DNA, measured in six DNA-brush clusters from two slides, with supplied ribosomes. A complete, jointly self-producing translation module remains open.
milestones.set_by: Rothschild et al.’s 2024 roadmap, Box 2, stage 2, endorsed by Build-a-Cell.
milestones.threshold_quote: ribosomes making ribosomes, and the rest of the translation apparatus

milestones.title: A cell-free gene-expression system regenerates itself through repeated cycles.
milestones.criterion: The transcription–translation system, which reads genes and synthesizes proteins, regenerates itself through repeated operating cycles. The roadmap leaves the cycle count unspecified. Lavickova et al., published on 11 December 2020, demonstrated partial regeneration of up to seven aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases, enzymes that attach amino acids to transfer RNAs. Their microfluidic device contained eight 15 nL reactors operated at 34 °C, replacing 20% of each reaction every 15 minutes. Other machinery, ribosomes and DNA templates were supplied.
milestones.set_by: Rothschild et al.’s 2024 roadmap, Box 2, stage 3, endorsed by Build-a-Cell.

milestones.title: A synthetic cell maintains its own machinery for growth, DNA replication and division.
milestones.criterion: Growth, genome replication and division are coordinated within one synthetic cell-like system, with the required molecular machinery encoded and maintained by the cell itself. BaSyC publishes this qualitative target. Biotic’s developer summary of the 2026 SpudCell preprint reports five generations of selection, recurring delivery of enzymes and ribosomes in feeder liposomes, and division assisted by external streptavidin and linker proteins. The SpudCell results are not peer reviewed.
milestones.set_by: BaSyC, the Dutch Gravitation-funded Building a Synthetic Cell programme, Research Strategy, integration and autonomy objective.
milestones.threshold_quote: the molecular machinery required for these processes is encoded and maintained by the cell itself.

not_found: The SynCell Asia journal article exposed subscription-preview text, so its numerical endpoint is sourced to the coordinating academy’s announcement.
The Gaut preprint returned HTTP 403, and its author-hosted PDF exceeded the browser’s size limit.
Searches of Build-a-Cell, BaSyC and SynCell Asia materials found no shared serial-dilution or initial-machinery carryover threshold.

results.detail: New plasmid DNA was measured after digestion of the original DNA. Each generation used feeder liposomes and mechanical division.
results.quote: Newly synthesized DNA was detected in cells after each generation.

results.finding: Synthetic cells with a 90 kbp genome combined feeding, DNA replication and division; sample size not stated for this experiment.
results.detail: Feeder liposomes supplied enzymes and ribosomes, and division required externally added streptavidin and a linker. The separate five-generation experiment used mechanical division.
results.quote: This experiment demonstrated that synthetic minimal cells with 90kbp genome can undergo both genetically encoded growth and division.

results.finding: Across eight biological replicates, 2.9% ± 1.3% of liposomes showed both DNA replication and lipid synthesis.

results.finding: EF-Tu and IF3 were co-regenerated for up to 20 rounds; sample size not stated.
results.detail: The result covers two translation factors. The text does not report synthesis of functional ribosomes or the complete translation apparatus.
results.quote: We further extended this framework to the co-regeneration of multiple translation factors and demonstrated sustainable co-regeneration of EF-Tu and IF3, another major essential translation protein, for up to 20 rounds.

results.finding: EF-Tu and IF3 were co-regenerated for up to 20 rounds; sample size not stated.
results.detail: Repeated regeneration of two translation factors is reported, but regeneration of the complete transcription–translation system is not demonstrated.
results.quote: We further extended this framework to the co-regeneration of multiple translation factors and demonstrated sustainable co-regeneration of EF-Tu and IF3, another major essential translation protein, for up to 20 rounds.

results.finding: PURE synthesized 36 non-ribosome proteins in one reaction; functional assays used 2 technical replicates.
results.detail: The purified proteins reconstituted a functional expression system with supplied ribosomes. Functional synthesis of every individual protein was not established.
results.quote: Finally, we show that all 36 non-ribosome PURE proteins can be synthesized simultaneously in a single PURE reaction and, after purification, can reconstitute a functional PURE system.

results.finding: Single-reaction PURE protein regeneration achieved 8% efficiency; functional assays used 2 technical replicates.
results.detail: Purified proteins reconstituted a functional second-generation system, but sustained regeneration across repeated cycles was not demonstrated. Ribosomes were supplied.
results.quote: Therefore, the regeneration efficiency of the system is 8%, which aligns with our previous estimates that the synthesis capacity of the original PURE system is at least an order of magnitude lower than what is required for sustained self-regeneration of all non-ribosome proteins

results.finding: Nascent ribosomal subunits produced functional ribosomes in three independent experiments.
results.detail: The subunits were produced in E. coli extract with supplied native ribosomes, then purified and mixed for the activity test. The remaining translation machinery was not shown to regenerate.
results.quote: We observed translational activity under the double-antibiotic condition only when we mixed the purified nascent artificial SSU and LSU.
